s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction with highly vascularized mass
salient_findings: Voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
Hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Considerable uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy regarding rib and vertebral lesions
key_facts: Woman in her 30s with no relevant medical history
Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction
Endoscopic examination found a voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
CT scan showed a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, on the left thyroid, the fifth rib, and the L4 vertebra
MRI confirmed a hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Radioiodine scintigraphy found considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions
Sinonasal tumor had low uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy
Serum thyroglobulin was significantly elevated at 4432 ng/mL
Biopsy results confirmed VTC metastasis in both costal and sinonasal tumor biopsies

raw.rationale: The presence of metastasis in the nasal cavity, ribs, and vertebra, along with significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin and confirmation of VTC metastasis in biopsy results, points towards a thyroid cancer with metastatic potential. Papillary thyroid carcinoma is known for its ability to metastasize to distant sites, including bones and other unusual locations like the nasal cavity.

rejected.label: Follicular thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: Less likely to metastasize to unusual sites like the nasal cavity compared to papillary thyroid carcinoma

rejected.label: Tall cell variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: While aggressive, the primary diagnosis of papillary thyroid carcinoma is more encompassing and explains the metastatic pattern

rejected.label: Columnar cell variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: A rare and aggressive variant, but the information provided does not specifically suggest characteristics unique to this variant

rejected.label: Hürthle cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Typically has a different metastatic pattern and the biopsy results and clinical presentation do not specifically suggest Hürthle cell features
